title: The Lighthouse Keeper’s Daughter
author: Tadoku Note (original)
summary: 嵐の夜、灯台守の父は町へ出たまま戻れません。灯台の明かりが消えたとき、12歳のネルが取った行動とは。

source.note: Original text written for this app.

paragraphs: Nell lived on a small island with her father. There were no other people on the island. There were only rocks, birds, the sea and a tall white lighthouse. Nell’s father was the lighthouse keeper. Every night, he climbed the one hundred and twelve steps to the top and made sure the big lamp was burning. The light told ships, “Danger! Rocks here! Stay away!”

Nell was twelve. She knew every rock on the island and every bird’s name. She knew how to row a boat and how to tie strong knots. She also knew how the lamp worked, because she often helped her father.

One morning in October, her father said, “Nell, I must go to the town today. I need oil for the lamp and food for us. I will be back before dark.” He got into the little boat and rowed away. Nell waved until she could not see him.

In the afternoon, the sky turned dark gray. The wind began to blow. The sea became wild, and big waves hit the rocks. Nell stood at the window and looked toward the town. There was no boat. The sea was too dangerous. Her father could not come back.
Night came. The storm was getting worse. Nell was alone, and she was afraid. Then she thought of the lamp. Somebody had to light it. And there was nobody but her.
She took a small lamp and started to climb the stairs. One hundred and twelve steps. The wind screamed outside, and the tower shook a little. Her legs were tired, but she did not stop.

At the top, she did everything her father did. She cleaned the glass. She checked the oil. There was not much oil, only enough for one night, she thought. She lit the lamp. Then she turned the handle to make the light go around. Slowly, the big light began to turn. Its beam went out over the black, angry sea.
Every few hours, the machine slowed down, and Nell had to turn the handle again. She did not sleep. She sat by the lamp and listened to the storm.

At about three o’clock in the morning, she saw something through the rain. A small light. Then another. It was a ship! It was close to the island, very close to the rocks. Nell held her breath. Could they see her light?

Slowly, the ship turned. It moved away from the rocks and out into the open sea. Nell watched it until its lights disappeared. Then she sat down on the floor and cried. She was not sad. She was just very, very tired.
In the morning, the storm stopped. The sea was calm and blue. At ten o’clock, she saw two boats coming from the town. One was her father’s. The other was a big boat with a lot of people in it.
Her father ran up the beach and held her in his arms. “Nell! You’re safe! Did you... was it you? Did you light the lamp?”

A man in a blue coat came up to them. He was the captain of the ship. “Last night we were lost in the storm,” he said. “We could not see anything. Then we saw your light. You saved my ship and twenty-six men.”
The people from the town clapped and cheered. Nell’s face turned red.

That evening, Nell and her father climbed the stairs together. One hundred and twelve steps. At the top, her father gave her a small brass key. “This is the key to the lamp room,” he said. “Every keeper has one. Now you have one too.”
Nell kept that key all her life. Many years later, she became the keeper of the lighthouse herself.
